newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico tourism revenues jump to $7 bln in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Mexico tourism revenues jump to $7 bln in 1996.

text.p: Mexico received about 22 million visitors in 1996, generating $7.0 billion in income, compared with $6.317 billion in 1995, Tourism Secretary Silvia Hernandez said.
"Banco de Mexico (the central bank) has estimated that in 1996 tourism will give Mexico $7 billion dollars in currency, 13 percent more than the year before," Hernandez said.
She said that about 22 million visitors came to Mexico in 1996, 30 percent more than in 1995. The most popular tourist spots were Cancun, Los Cabos and Puerto Vallarta.

Vehicle rental agencies also reported a good recovery last year. Enrique Alvarez, president of the Association of Vehicle Renters, said some 15,000 vehicles were rented in 1996, 4,605 above the last count in 1993.
